card.how_to_use_the_feature_semantics: each entry gives the formula and the window it is computed on.  Three scopes are different objects and the vocabulary only covers the first: the feature window is the whole observed history; the serving window is its last 192 points and is the only thing the Consumer sees; the modified region is whatever the program actually changes at execution time, and no feature here measures it.  A threshold you write is therefore a statement about the whole history, not about the window that will be served and not about the region that will be changed.  Nothing here tells you how a value moves from one window to the next -- that is not recorded and you should not assume it.

proposal.written_text: When forecast evidence shows both substantial missingness and a strong local robust deviation, inspect the missingness and deviation regions separately. Treat a broad or uncertain deviation span as insufficient public evidence for an outlier repair, because the observed negative cases include missing_fraction above 0.4 and local_robust_z_peak above 5 while the same mechanism also has mixed outcomes elsewhere. Prefer a minimal localized program only when the inspected hypothesis has a legal verifiable binding; otherwise retain identity. Keep the existing behavior for cases without this combined evidence and for narrowly localized deviations with sufficient public support.
predicted_data_effect: For forecast contexts meeting the combined public-evidence condition, fewer broad outlier repairs should be selected when inspection cannot establish a localized, legally bound deviation hypothesis.
Contexts without the combined condition should preserve the existing inspection and candidate-selection behavior.
falsification_condition: In subsequent matched contexts satisfying task_kind == forecast, missing_fraction >= 0.4, and local_robust_z_peak >= 5, the retrieved guidance does not increase explicit identity retention when the inspected deviation region is broad or uncertain.
